title: Concrete Fence Wall on Twin Helical Piles (Medium Sand, Partial Water Table)
description:
A 6-ft tall, 6-in thick reinforced concrete fence wall is supported at 6-ft on-center by pairs of helical piles (2 piles per support, 3 ft apart) with 12-in diameter helix plates. The backfill is medium dense sand (φ = 32°, γ = 115 pcf, γsat = 125 pcf). A surcharge of q = 100 psf acts at the ground surface, and the water table sits hw = 2 ft above the base.

Determine:
1. The Rankine active pressure coefficient Ka and total lateral force V per support.
2. The overturning moment M at grade for this support.
3. The compression- and tension-side axial demand on the pile couple (arm = 3 ft).
4. The ultimate helical pile bearing capacity Qult at the 8-ft embedment depth, and whether the sliding (≥1.5), overturning (≥2.0), and pile bearing/pullout (≥3.0) safety factors are satisfied.
hint: Compute Ka from φ=32°. Break the lateral pressure into the dry-zone triangle, the submerged rectangle (from dry overburden), the submerged buoyant triangle, the surcharge rectangle, and the hydrostatic pore-water triangle. Sum forces × tributary spacing S=6 ft for V, and sum (force × arm) × S for M. For the 2-pile couple, T = M/arm ± (self-weight/2).
shortcut: For a 2-pile moment-resisting foundation, the governing check is almost always pile bearing/pullout (FS≥3.0) rather than sliding, because the couple arm is short relative to the moment — widening the pile spacing or upsizing the helix diameter is far more effective than adding embedment depth once the shaft is already resisting lateral shear adequately.
fifthGrader: Imagine the wall is trying to fall over like a book pushed from the side. Two big screws (helical piles) are driven into the ground under it — one gets squeezed (compression) and the other gets pulled up (tension) like a seesaw, and together they hold the wall from tipping over!

title: Wood Fence Post on a Single Helical Pile (Stiff Clay, No Water Table)
description:
A 5-ft tall wood fence (6×6 treated timber posts at 6-ft spacing) is supported by a single 10-in diameter helical pile per post, embedded 6 ft into stiff clay (φ = 0°, c = 1000 psf, γ = 115 pcf). No groundwater is present and there is no surface surcharge.

Determine:
1. The lateral force and moment demand at grade for one post.
2. The 6×6 post's actual bending stress fb and its ratio to the allowable Fb = 1350 psi.
3. Since a single pile cannot form a moment couple, show how the pile's embedded shaft resists the overturning moment through passive soil pressure, and compute the resulting overturning safety factor.
4. Comment on why a single-pile foundation typically requires more embedment depth than an equivalent 2-pile system for the same wall height.
hint: With φ=0 (undrained clay), Ka=1.0, so the active pressure is just the equivalent-fluid triangle plus any cohesive relief (neglected here for simplicity). A single embedded pile resists moment the same way a direct-burial post does: passive soil pressure builds up along the shaft, with the resultant of the triangular pressure block acting at 2D/3 below grade.
shortcut: Whenever numPiles = 1, watch the 'Pile Bearing/Pullout FS' card — it only reflects the pile's small axial dead-load capacity (very high FS, not meaningful) because there's no moment couple. The 'Overturning FS' card is the one that actually governs a single-pile foundation.
fifthGrader: With just one screw in the ground, the fence post has to lean on the dirt around it to keep from tipping — like sticking a pencil deep into sand so it doesn't fall over when you push the top. The deeper it goes, the more sand pushes back to hold it up!

title: Fiberglass Fence on a 3-Pile Helical Group (Loose Sand, High Water Table)
description:
An 8-ft tall fiberglass (pultruded FRP) privacy fence uses 8×8 FRP tube posts at 5-ft spacing, each supported by a 3-pile helical group (piles at 4-ft spacing, 16-in diameter helices) embedded 12 ft into loose sand (φ = 28°, γ = 105 pcf, γsat = 118 pcf). The water table is high, at hw = 6 ft above the base, and a 150 psf surcharge acts at grade.

Determine:
1. The effect of the high water table on both the lateral demand (buoyant unit weight, pore pressure) and the pile capacity (reduced effective stress at the helix depth).
2. The FRP post's flexural stress ratio against its allowable Fb = 15,000 psi.
3. For the 3-pile group (couple arm = 2 × 4 ft = 8 ft), the compression- and tension-side pile demands.
4. Whether FS = 3.0 uniform-target mode (rather than the fixed 1.5/2.0/3.0 mapping) is satisfied by this configuration, and what single change (diameter, spacing, or pile count) would most efficiently close the gap if it is not.
hint: Loose sand plus a high water table is a demanding combination: buoyant unit weight γ' = γsat - 62.4 reduces both the lateral resisting friction and the pile's effective bearing stress, while the hydrostatic thrust adds directly to the lateral demand. For 3 piles, the outer two form the primary couple (arm = 2×pileSpacing); the center pile mainly carries vertical share.
shortcut: A saturated loose-sand + high water table case is exactly when you should reach for a larger helix diameter rather than more embedment depth — capacity scales with the helix bearing area (∝ D²), while lateral/embedment resistance only helps the sliding and overturning checks, not the governing pile bearing/pullout check.
fifthGrader: When the ground gets really wet and squishy like a water balloon, everything under the fence gets lighter and weaker at the same time water pushes harder from the side. That's why this fence needs three big screws working together — with wide screw plates — to stay standing safely!
